meta.title: LingoLinq Capability Ledger
meta.purpose: Code-cited, present-tense source of truth for what the product actually does today, so compliance docs (and reviewers) ground claims against verified capabilities instead of re-deriving them by hand. citation-check.rb is to findings as capability-check.rb (Phase B) is to this ledger.
meta.canonicalWhen: Enforced as of Phase B: scripts/capability-check.rb validates every built/partial row's currentEvidence at HEAD and every deliberately-not-done row's negativeEvidence in CI (audit-artifacts-integrity). Mirroring to external tools (e.g. Codex AGENTS.md) is now permissible for these code-cited, identifier-free rows.

evidenceSemantics.currentEvidence: file:line:snippet that MUST resolve at HEAD (the current checkout), not a pinned SHA. Proves the capability is STILL true today. Required for status built/partial.
evidenceSemantics.introducedEvidence: optional provenance only (when/where a capability landed); NOT validated; may reference a historical SHA.
evidenceSemantics.negativeEvidence: scoped proof of absence for deliberately-not-done rows: grep scopes, patterns, excluded paths, reviewed surfaces, expectedMatches, and a re-review trigger. Phase B re-runs the greps at HEAD and fails if the match count diverges from expectedMatches.
evidenceSemantics.framing: deliberately-not-done rows describe out-of-scope-by-design choices, never known-gaps-shipped-without.

capabilities.capability: Password authentication (bcrypt-hashed, via the passwords concern / GoSecure)
capabilities.claimLanguage: Accounts are protected by password authentication with hashed credentials.
capabilities.notes: Password verification lives in app/models/concerns/passwords.rb; Google OAuth and SAML SSO also exist as alternative sign-in paths.

capabilities.claimLanguage: Two-factor authentication (TOTP) is available to users.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT mandatory; do not claim enforced MFA for all users or admins.
capabilities.notes: Open item: make admin/staff 2FA mandatory (tracked separately). Optional today.

capabilities.capability: Server-side at-rest encryption of sensitive fields (secure_serialize / SECURE_ENCRYPTION_KEY)
capabilities.claimLanguage: Sensitive fields are encrypted at rest server-side.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT end-to-end encryption; LingoLinq holds the keys. Do not claim 'zero readable keys' or E2EE.
capabilities.notes: Encryption keys are held by the application. This is server-side encryption, distinct from E2EE (see cap no-e2ee).

capabilities.capability: PiiScrubber pseudonymizes (scrubs direct identifiers from) payloads before AI egress
capabilities.claimLanguage: Only pseudonymized (scrubbed) data is sent to AI subprocessors; it remains personal data under GDPR/UK-GDPR.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT de-identified or anonymized. Pseudonymized data is still personal data; does not meet HIPAA Safe Harbor.
capabilities.notes: Scrubber removes known direct identifiers (patterns + configured blocklist). NER coverage is an open limitation; free-hand third-party names can evade it.

capabilities.capability: COPPA hard-gate blocks AI generation for under-13 users awaiting parental consent
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI features are blocked for under-13 users until verifiable parental consent is captured.
capabilities.antiClaim: This is an under-13 (COPPA) gate; it does NOT itself enforce an EU under-16 (GDPR Art. 8) block on the AI path (see cap eu-under16-ai-block).
capabilities.notes: Gate is FeatureFlags.coppa_blocks_ai_for?(user); enforced at both AI generator call sites.

capabilities.capability: Jurisdiction detection primitive (EU vs non-EU) exists
capabilities.claimLanguage: The platform can determine whether an account context is in the EU.
capabilities.antiClaim: The EU jurisdiction primitive gates the Art. 50(1) disclosure modal (built and staged, gated OFF behind the article_50_disclosure flag; see cap art50-1-disclosure-modal) and, via the Phase 4 call-context helper, stamps jurisdiction on AiApiLog rows; it does not by itself drive an under-16 AI block.

introducedEvidence.note: lib/eu_jurisdiction.rb (module EuJurisdiction, line 12); PRs #556/#560. Consumed by LingoLinq::Article50CallContext.for at the three AI call sites (Phase 4, PR #635).

capabilities.capability: EU AI Act Article 50(2) machine-readable output marking -- board-generation slice only
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI board-generation output is marked in a machine-readable, server-verifiable way (Art. 50(2)).
capabilities.antiClaim: The Art. 50(2) obligation is NOT closed: this slice marks board generation ONLY. Other AI-output surfaces (generate_focus_words, AiWordPredictor.predict, eval narration, AiPredictionGenerator) are not yet marked, and durable persistence of the marker (board.settings + relinking copy_for) is follow-up. capabilities.capability: Full hard-delete of a user on request (flush_user_completely)

capabilities.capability: AI board generation + word prediction via Anthropic Claude on AWS Bedrock (Anthropic-only runtime); code path built, NOT operational in production
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI features (board generation and word prediction) are implemented against Anthropic Claude on AWS Bedrock. They are not operational in production as of 2026-08-04: no currently deployed revision carries a Bedrock credential, so the features degrade to their 'AI is not configured' path. The Bedrock path was configured once, from 2026-08-03T08:23Z to 2026-08-04T06:31Z (revision 00013-76w). In that window WORD PREDICTION was exercised: one call completed, an internal verification call carrying no user or student data. BOARD GENERATION and PREDICTION SEEDING were reachable (both resolve to anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5, the one alias mapped on the classic plane) but were NOT exercised; no call by either is recorded in AiApiLog. Reachable is a configuration statement, not an observation.
capabilities.antiClaim: Do NOT claim these AI features are live or available to users today; they are code-complete but unconfigured in production as of 2026-08-04 (credentials withdrawn on revision 00014-5rw). Equally, do NOT claim they have never been operational: the path was configured from 2026-08-03T08:23Z to 2026-08-04T06:31Z on revision 00013-76w. Do NOT say all the features 'ran' in that window: only word prediction completed a call. Board generation and prediction seeding were reachable but unexercised, and eval narration was unavailable throughout (Opus 4.7 has no classic-plane profile and the account is not mantle-entitled). No user or student data was transmitted in that window. See the 2026-08-04 operational-status correction in docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md. The prior Google Gemini fallback was DISABLED 2026-07-09 (Gemini Developer/AI-Studio endpoint data-handling terms inadequate for child data); there is no runtime Gemini path today. When configured, runtime AI egresses to Claude on AWS Bedrock via lib/ai_client.rb, not the direct api.anthropic.com endpoint; enforced in CI by scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh. AWS exposes two Bedrock planes and AiClient supports both, selected by BEDROCK_PLANE: classic bedrock-runtime (the default, and the only plane this account is entitled to as of 2026-08-01) and bedrock-mantle (403 'not available for this account' on every model even with admin credentials; access request open with AWS). Both planes are inside the AWS account BAA boundary, so plane selection is an entitlement/routing matter, not a data-protection one. Only pseudonymized data is sent (see cap pii-scrubber-pseudonymization).

introducedEvidence.note: Bedrock routing switch (lib/ai_client.rb, AiClient.build) recorded in docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md + docs/legal/ANTHROPIC_BAA_ACCEPTED.md 2026-07-24; Gemini fallback removal in docs/legal/AI_DATA_SHARING_CONSENT.md section 2.2 and docs/legal/AI_GOVERNANCE_MEMO.md

capabilities.notes: Runtime constructs the sanctioned Claude client via AiClient.build; no direct Anthropic client or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY read on the runtime seams (CI guard scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh). Downgraded built -> partial on 2026-08-01: currentEvidence proves the code path exists at HEAD, but the feature does not run in production. Status re-verified 2026-08-04 and held at partial. History: no Bedrock credential was present on revisions 00001-2vn (2026-06-29) through 00012-x8z (2026-08-02), so AiClient.configured? was false throughout. PRs #719 (BEDROCK_AWS_* mount) and #727 (classic-plane default) landed, and revision 00013-76w (2026-08-03T08:23:02Z) mounted the credentials. During that window the AWS_BAA verification standard was met for the first time: a mounted Bedrock credential on the serving revision AND sts:GetCallerIdentity under it returning account 239044785114 (principal user/lingolinq-bedrock-runtime), plus a successful live AiWordPredictor.predict call logged to AiApiLog at 2026-08-04T05:44:42Z. Credentials were then deliberately withdrawn on revision 00014-5rw (2026-08-04T06:31:46Z), so the capability is again not operational and remains partial rather than built. Restoring status=built requires re-mounting the credential and re-meeting the same two-part standard on the then-serving revision. On the classic plane the wire id is a cross-region inference-profile id; eval narration requests Opus 4.7, which the classic catalog does not carry, so it remains on its deterministic template fallback. Subprocessors listed in docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md; that register's Gemini row may need a runtime-status update to reflect the 2026-07-09 disable (flagged separately, not fixed here).

capabilities.capability: Message banking retains the user's OWN voice recordings for playback
capabilities.claimLanguage: Message banking stores a user's own recorded messages for playback.
capabilities.antiClaim: These are the user's own communication recordings, NOT voiceprints/speaker-ID/biometrics (see cap no-voiceprints).
capabilities.notes: Most sensitive data category (health-adjacent, ALS use). A temp WAV made only for auto-transcribing a text label is deleted; the banked recording is retained by design.

capabilities.capability: Signed AWS Business Associate Agreement (HIPAA-eligible AWS services in use)
capabilities.claimLanguage: A signed BAA is in place with AWS covering HIPAA-eligible services under the BAA'd account, including S3 storage in active use and Amazon Bedrock, which is the designated runtime AI inference path.
capabilities.antiClaim: Do NOT claim Bedrock inference is in use today: the BAA covers it, but no Bedrock call is made from production as of 2026-08-04 (no credential mounted on the current revision 00014-5rw). One word-prediction call did complete during the closed window 2026-08-03T08:23Z to 2026-08-04T06:31Z on 00013-76w, so do NOT state this as 'never'; see the 2026-08-04 operational-status correction in docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md. Do NOT cite the retracted 2026-07-27 claim as evidence that the operative condition (calls signed under account 2390-4478-5114) was verified; it was false when made and stays retracted. The condition WAS verified once, on 2026-08-04, during the closed 00013-76w window (sts:GetCallerIdentity returned 2390-4478-5114, principal user/lingolinq-bedrock-runtime). Cite that dated verification, not the retracted one, and note it lapsed when credentials were withdrawn on 00014-5rw; it must be re-verified on any future mount. The AWS BAA does NOT cover a direct third-party model endpoint outside AWS (e.g. api.anthropic.com). That direct path is unused at runtime today; when used it is covered by the Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA (see cap anthropic-model-provider-baa). Fable/Mythos models are excluded from Bedrock HIPAA eligibility.

capabilities.capability: EU AI Act Article 50(1) user-facing AI-interaction disclosure modal
capabilities.claimLanguage: An accessible EU-gated AI-interaction disclosure modal, an acknowledgement endpoint, and a shared first-AI-use gate are built and staged.
capabilities.antiClaim: Built and staged, but gated OFF: the `article_50_disclosure` frontend flag is registered in AVAILABLE_FRONTEND_FEATURES only (not enabled for any user), so the modal is shown to no one yet. Do not claim a LIVE or enabled Art. 50(1) disclosure in production. Enabling the flag was the 2026-08-02 release gate, on Scot's sign-off, after the production deploy. GATE STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-04: that date has passed and the flag is still AVAILABLE-only, so it is shown to no one. The production deploy occurred (revision 00012-x8z, 2026-08-02T20:31Z) and runtime AI subsequently became operational on revision 00013-76w (2026-08-03T08:23Z to 2026-08-04T06:31Z). During that ~22h window the product was performing AI interactions with the Article 50(1) disclosure disabled. Exposure was limited: the only call in the window was an internal verification call with no end user involved, and credentials have since been withdrawn, so no user encountered an undisclosed AI interaction. This gate is now OVERDUE and must be closed before any future credential mount, not after. Enabling a user-facing flag is Scot's decision and is deliberately not auto-applied here.

capabilities.notes: Disclosure content (lib/lingo_linq/ai_consent_disclosures.rb, Phase 2), Ember modal + ack endpoint + gate (Phase 3), and jurisdiction stamping (Phase 4, cap jurisdiction-primitive) are all built and on staging. Inert until the flag is enabled. EU clock 2026-08-02.

capabilities.capability: Zero-data-retention (ZDR) confirmed for the two in-scope Anthropic models ON THE DIRECT api.anthropic.com PATH ONLY (not the Bedrock runtime route)
capabilities.claimLanguage: The two in-scope Anthropic models (Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Opus 4.7) are ZDR-confirmed per Anthropic's data-retention documentation (verified 2026-07-06) WHEN ACCESSED OVER THE DIRECT ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL API. Scoped 2026-08-04: that path is not the runtime route. The designated runtime route is Claude on AWS Bedrock, where retention is governed by the AWS account BAA and AWS service terms; no ZDR guarantee is claimed for the Bedrock path.
capabilities.antiClaim: Do NOT cite this row as a ZDR guarantee for the AWS Bedrock runtime route; it is scoped to the direct api.anthropic.com path, which is not in runtime use. The shipped runtime disclosure (privacy.hbs, lib/lingo_linq/ai_consent_disclosures.rb) explicitly states that no zero-data-retention guarantee is claimed for the Bedrock path, and this ledger row must not contradict it. ZDR is confirmed ONLY for these two specific models; it does NOT extend to any other/future Anthropic model outside the ZDR-eligible tier, and NOT to any non-Anthropic provider. ZDR is NOT a substitute for a HIPAA BAA (see cap anthropic-model-provider-baa for the executed Anthropic BAA and cap aws-s3-baa for Bedrock under the AWS BAA). Fable 5 / Mythos-class models are explicitly NOT ZDR-eligible and never receive identifiable payloads.
capabilities.notes: Confirmed against Anthropic Privacy Center data-retention documentation, not a bespoke signed ZDR addendum. Reverify on any runtime model change.

capabilities.capability: Signed BAA covering the AI model-provider (Anthropic) egress path
capabilities.claimLanguage: A signed Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA covers the Anthropic model-provider path. Runtime AI is coded to route to Claude on AWS Bedrock under the AWS account BAA instead, and is not operational in production as of 2026-08-04, having been operational only from 2026-08-03T08:23Z to 2026-08-04T06:31Z for internal verification.
capabilities.antiClaim: Do NOT claim there is active runtime AI egress on any path today: the direct api.anthropic.com route is disabled and no current revision mounts a Bedrock credential, so no runtime model egress occurs (see the 2026-08-04 operational-status correction in docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md). Do NOT cite the retracted 2026-07-27 claim as evidence the Bedrock operative condition was verified; that claim was false when made and was retracted. The condition WAS independently verified for the first time on 2026-08-04 (sts:GetCallerIdentity returning 239044785114 under the mounted credential), during the closed operational window only; cite that dated verification rather than the retracted one. Google (Gemini) as a model provider still has no BAA; its runtime fallback remains disabled (2026-07-09). The Anthropic BAA is the still-available direct-path basis, not the active Bedrock route.
capabilities.notes: Supersedes the former deliberately-not-done cap no-model-provider-baa. Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA executed 2026-07-18; runtime routing moved to Bedrock 2026-07-24 under the AWS BAA. Id retained as anthropic-model-provider-baa so inbound references to the closed gap resolve. CORRECTED 2026-08-01: this row previously asserted 'Operative conditions verified 2026-07-27: the deployed Cloud Run service lingolinq-web signs Bedrock with a credential that resolves to the BAA'd AWS account 2390-4478-5114 (us-west-2) ... (residual: shared app AWS credential, not a dedicated Bedrock credential)'. That is retracted. No lingolinq-web revision from 00001-2vn through 00012-x8z carried a Bedrock credential, which is the period the retracted claim covered; BEDROCK_AWS_KEY/SECRET were first mounted on 00013-76w (2026-08-03T08:23:02Z) and withdrawn on 00014-5rw (2026-08-04T06:31:46Z), and the operative condition was verified once in that window on 2026-08-04. The parenthetical was the root error: AWS_KEY/AWS_SECRET are the S3/SES pair and AiClient.aws_credentials deliberately does NOT read them for Bedrock, so a 'shared app AWS credential' could never have signed a Bedrock call. The separate finding that Bedrock model-invocation logging is OFF in 2390-4478-5114/us-west-2 was verified in-account, independently of the deployment, and still stands.
